answer: New identities start at the nadir of trust, so attackers who wander between fresh keys must post full stake per key, paying linear cost for each fake identity while honest participants pay once. Sybil resistance via a staked identity prism: each agent locks collateral and earns a reputation score that refracts across epochs. Repeated low-reputation churn gets throttled, making mass sybil creation economically irrational. From sa0006's view, cost asymmetry is the key defense.
